newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia liberalization seen boosting coal output.
newsitem.headline: Colombia liberalization seen boosting coal output.

text.p: Colombian coal production could be set to jump in the next few years as liberalization sweeps across the sector, government officials and foreign investors said on Tuesday.
At current rates of extraction, Colombia has more than three centuries' worth of high-quality reserves, they said.
Energy and Mines Minister Rodrigo Villamizar told delegates at an energy conference in Cartagena that the government planned nearly to double coal output from 24 to 40 million tonnes per year.
"We could double production with a relatively minor effort to improve infrastructure," he said.
A new mining code approved last year, which allowed repatriation of mining proceeds, among other measures, would speed foreign investment in the sector, he added.

Colombia is liberalizing its coal sector, with plans this year to sell its 50 percent stake in Cerrejon Norte mine, which produces 15 million tonnes a year, and to offer four exploration licences in the northern Guajira region.
Colombian government officials at the conference said the deadline for the licensing round was May 16, while the privatisation would be ready in the first half of this year.

Mike Tracy, president of U.S. coal-mining company Drummond, said Colombia could provide a large part of an increase in demand of 30 million tonnes forecast for Europe and the Americas in the next five years.
Obstacles to growth were the limited rail and port infrastructure, but Colombia's rail capacity should rise to 28 million tonnes this year, he added.
"The cost of transportation and port operations account for over 50 percent of the cost of Colombian coal exports," he added.
As for Drummond's Colombian coal output, Tracy expected it to rise from 4.1 million tonnes in 1996 to 5.2 million next year, reaching 10 million tonnes by 2000.
Colombia had an "excellent business environment," he said, adding that Drummond was participating in the current licensing round to acquire more reserves.
